A communication unit receives an original video signal that includes information representing the original video content. This original video signal is then provided to a controller, which processes the signal by delaying the original video by a first predetermined time period. As a result, the controller generates a delayed video signal corresponding to the original video signal shifted in time.

The communication unit also transmits the original video signal to a subtitler terminal. The subtitler terminal uses the original video signal to prepare subtitle information corresponding to the video content. In addition, the subtitler terminal generates subtitle delay information indicating a delay associated with the creation, transmission, or timing of the subtitle information. The subtitler terminal then returns both the subtitle information and the subtitle delay information.

Based on the subtitle delay information, the controller generates a display timing signal. The display timing signal is used to determine when the subtitle information should be displayed in synchronization with the delayed video signal. In this way, the subtitles can be presented at appropriate times while the viewer watches the delayed version of the original video.

The communication unit then transmits the delayed video signal, the subtitle information, and the display timing signal to a viewer terminal. The viewer terminal uses these signals to display the delayed video together with the corresponding subtitles according to the display timing signal, thereby enabling the subtitles to be synchronized with the video presented to the viewer.

A video delivery method is provided for synchronizing subtitles with video content when the video content is intentionally delayed before being delivered to a viewer. In this method, an original video signal is first received by a video delivery system. The system applies a delay to the original video, thereby producing a delayed video signal that will later be transmitted to a viewer terminal.

The original video, before or while being delayed, is sent to a subtitler terminal. At the subtitler terminal, an operator or an automatic subtitle generation system creates subtitle data corresponding to speech, audio, or events contained in the original video. The subtitler terminal also provides subtitle delay information indicating a delay associated with the creation, processing, or transmission of the subtitle data.

The video delivery system receives the subtitle data and the subtitle delay information from the subtitler terminal. Based on the subtitle delay information and the amount of delay applied to the original video, the system generates subtitle display timing information. This timing information specifies when each subtitle should be displayed in relation to the delayed video so that the subtitles appear at the correct time during playback.

The system then transmits the delayed video signal to a viewer terminal together with the subtitle data and the generated subtitle display timing information. At the viewer terminal, the delayed video is played back, and the subtitles are displayed according to the synchronized timing information. As a result, even though the video has been delayed and the subtitles may have been generated after the original video was received, the subtitles are presented to the viewer at appropriate times corresponding to the relevant portions of the delayed video.

This method allows subtitles to be accurately synchronized with delayed video delivery, making it useful for live broadcasts, streaming services, remote captioning systems, and other video distribution environments in which subtitles must be generated or adjusted in real time.

**A Method for Turning Ideas into Results**

A method for achieving any goal begins with clarity. Before taking action, it is important to understand what you want to accomplish and why it matters. Clear goals provide direction, reduce confusion, and make it easier to measure progress.

The next step is planning. A good method involves breaking a large goal into smaller, manageable tasks. Each task should have a purpose, a deadline, and a clear outcome. This makes the process less overwhelming and helps maintain motivation over time.

After planning comes action. Even the best strategy is useless without consistent effort. Progress often happens through small steps repeated regularly. By focusing on one task at a time, it becomes easier to build momentum and avoid distractions.

Evaluation is also an important part of any method. Reviewing results helps identify what is working and what needs improvement. If something is not effective, adjustments can be made before too much time or energy is wasted.

Finally, persistence is essential. Challenges and setbacks are a normal part of any process. A strong method allows flexibility while keeping the main objective in focus. With clear goals, careful planning, consistent action, and regular evaluation, ideas can be transformed into meaningful results.
